Nadia Haddad (Legal Team Member), password sign-in in an isolated Playwright Chromium context; this agent played the Client's protocol legs (authorization request, PKCE exchange as a public client, /mcp calls).
scenarios.expected: The Client acts as the signed-in person within the selected Toolsets, scope and record access. Disconnect removes the grant and the next call is unauthorized. Allow stays disabled without a Toolset and scope; Read and write is absent when the organization is read-only. An expired consent link requires a fresh connection; disabled Clients and account groups are refused.
scenarios.actual: Signed out, Claude's authorization request (client_id https://claude.ai/oauth/mcp-oauth-client-metadata, redirect https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback) went to /auth/login, which offered Business Portal sign-in; after Sign in the consent page read "Claude wants to work in OpenLaw as you", Published identity https://claude.ai/oauth/mcp-oauth-client-metadata, Allowed Client, Nadia Haddad · Legal team member · nadia.haddad@helix.example, "What Claude may use", "Nothing is selected for you.", 11 Toolset checkboxes with no Guide checkbox, "How far Claude may go" with Read only and Read and write, "This Client can never see or change what you cannot." Allow stayed disabled with nothing, with a Toolset only and with Read only only; enabled with both. Claude Code's identity showed "Claude Code wants to work in OpenLaw as you" and "What Claude Code may use". With the organization Read-only, only Read only was offered; a request without write also offered only Read only. An altered link and a link reopened after more than ten minutes showed "This consent request has expired or changed. Start again from your Client." with no actions. Claude turned off mid-flow showed "This Client is off in the organization's Allowed Clients list." with Deny alone; a new request got HTTP 400 "Client is not on the enabled Allowed Clients list." Legal Users OAuth Clients off showed "OAuth Clients are off for your account type." with Deny alone. A registered Client deleted mid-flow showed "This Client is not on the organization's Allowed Clients list." with Deny alone. On the local lab an existing Claude grant, made on the consent page and exchanged with PKCE, got 401 with MCP off, with Legal Users OAuth Clients off and with Claude off, and 200 when each came back. Claude Code callbacks http://localhost:<port>/callback and http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback completed consent, the loopback return and a PKCE exchange (tools/list 200); a non-loopback and a wrong-path callback were refused with "Callback URL is not allowed for this Client." Connecting again with prompt=consent showed the page and the new choices replaced the grant (workspace/read → contracts/write). Connected Clients (Settings → Personal → API keys) listed Claude with Toolsets, Write or Read, Granted and Last used; Disconnect → "Revoke OAuth grant · This Client will lose access immediately. A new consent is needed to connect again." → Revoke left "No Client is connected." Help /help/connect-claude matched the article openlaw_docs_read returns (81 of 81 sentences).

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough, not a human user study. The live-provider rows rest on the batch owner's own claude.ai session as relayed by the coordinator, and on this agent's server-side reads.

Claude Code CLI live connection not run: the batch owner skipped it. Its consent page, published identity and both loopback callback forms were walked in the browser with this agent playing the Client's protocol legs.
LAN only over a trusted private HTTPS address with a corporate CA for Claude Code was not walked.
Claude Desktop and Cowork were not connected; the guide says they use the same remote connection.

The lab served the guide at the pinned commit (bundle contentSha256 b8107eb0…) in Help and openlaw_docs_read; the Help and Guide parity check compares those two. The repository guide 50532b15 differs in wording that this walk checked step by step (walkthrough.json conclusion).
The plain-HTTP LAN claim (no OAuth) rests on the operator walker's V-M41-PUBLIC rows and plain-http-oauth-refused.png, not on this walk.

Claude's add-connector messages for an unreachable :8443 address ("Couldn't reach this address", "No server responded at this URL") are from the batch owner's screenshots as reported by the coordinator.

The Instance-address pill read "Not reachable · Public IPv4 address" on the public lab because the API resolved the Funnel hostname through the host's Tailscale MagicDNS; the guide says the pill does not prove vendor reachability.
Reconnecting a Client with a live grant and no prompt=consent reuses the remembered consent without a page; Claude's requests carry prompt=consent and then show the page, as the guide describes.
